caption: The drawing depicts a rectangular woven textile with a bordered edge, primarily featuring shades of red, blue, and beige. The main field of the textile has an intricate symmetrical design consisting of large floral and botanical motifs arranged in a repeating grid-like pattern. Along the bottom edge of the textile, there is a decorative border with additional floral motifs, beneath which is a row of capitalized text that reads: "UNITED WE STAND DIVIDED WE FALL 1841." There are also vertical border patterns on the right edge of the textile. The fabric background is beige with the designs worked in red and blue, giving a two-tone appearance to the patterns. The textile's left and bottom edges have small fringes. Surrounding the illustration, the background is plain off-white with minor brownish stains and aging marks. Below the textile, handwritten text reads “Westchester County” on the left and “drawn by I. De Strangue” on the right.
title: Quilt
cluster: #22 — Domestic Textiles: Coverlets, Tablecloths, and Rugs
